storylines.title: France riots and European unrest
storylines.summary: French protests entered a third week with 320,000 marching Saturday and clashes in Paris and Marseille. French officials opened an attempted-murder probe over petrol bombs thrown at police. Violent cost-of-living protests also hit German cities.

events.text: France opens an attempted-murder investigation after petrol bombs are thrown at riot police at Saturday's protests; no arrests reported.
Germany's cost-of-living protests turn violent in Berlin, Hamburg and Frankfurt, with shops looted, the same day hundreds of thousands protest in France.
Police clash with masked rioters in Paris, Marseille and other cities after largely peaceful third-wave marches across France.
Macron bans 'illegitimate' protests; total ban in Marseille and Lyon, union-organised marches only elsewhere, museums closed Saturday.
France's 10-year borrowing costs reach 5% for the first time since 2002, the FT reports.
Macron accuses Trump and other foreign leaders of 'stupid comments' about the unrest as France readies for more protests this weekend.
France announces nightly curfews in Paris, Lyon and other cities for as long as necessary after the first quiet night.
EU regulators probe pro-Kremlin disinformation and the role of social platforms around the French riots, the FT reports.
Italy approves sending 500 troops to Milan after clashes and protests.

storylines.title: US-Ukraine rift over Starlink and strikes
storylines.summary: The US approved 500 Patriot missiles for Ukraine. The Oleshky truce has ended, Ukraine resumed strikes on Russian refineries despite Trump's pressure, and air raid alert apps in both countries were hit by cyberattacks.

events.text: Air raid alert apps in Ukraine and Russia are hit by cyberattacks after the truce ends; Ukraine blames Russia for fake nuclear warnings.
Ukraine resumes attacks on Russian oil refineries in defiance of Trump pressure, the Guardian reports; the Kremlin says Kyiv is ignoring US wishes.
Evacuees from Russian-occupied Oleshky reach Ukraine during a localized US-brokered ceasefire.
US approves sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine, with $2.1 billion to be paid by allies.
Russia fires three waves of ballistic missiles at Kyiv; Downing Street and Zelenskyy rebuke Witkoff for calling Putin a 'humanitarian'.
CNBC: Musk's clash with Ukraine accelerates demand for Starlink alternatives, but few exist.
Missiles hit Kyiv after Russia agrees in principle to resume peace talks; Trump says the world is 'the closest we've been' to ending the war.
Trump links his Russia sanctions waiver to the release of jailed American Stephen Hubbard.
Russia to send its first diesel tanker to the US on Thursday under the Trump deal.
Putin tells Witkoff he agrees in principle to resume trilateral talks; Russia releases American Stephen Hubbard.
Witkoff to present Putin an updated proposal in St. Petersburg Wednesday, a US official says; Kushner to join virtually.
Trump says 'I don't care how it's done' as he presses Ukraine to cut a peace deal.
WSJ reports Musk ordered a Starshield slowdown that Ukraine said hampered its response to Russian attacks.
Hegseth says US posture toward Ukraine is unchanged but US forces also need Patriot interceptors.
Zelenskyy says US intelligence on missile strikes 'works now' after Oslo talks with Witkoff.
Witkoff meets Zelenskyy before travelling to Russia, the FT reports; Zelenskyy says missile-strike intelligence 'works now'.
Republicans push back on Trump's softer Russia stance; Rubio tells Zelenskyy Trump issued no order to harm Ukraine.
Witkoff is traveling to Oslo for Tuesday talks with Zelenskyy and European leaders on a peace proposal, a US official says.
Zelenskyy lobbies a bipartisan group of senators to press the White House over alleged intelligence and weapons curbs.
Trump says Zelenskyy should nominate 'somebody else' to negotiate with Russia.

storylines.title: AI debt worries and market selloff
storylines.summary: Tech stocks ended the week lower as Big Tech earnings reignited AI spending fears, and credit investors describe a junk debt rout. The FT says the global AI selloff is easing after the Nasdaq's worst month in over a year, with US futures higher.

events.text: FT says the global AI selloff eases after the Nasdaq's worst month in over a year; US stock futures gain in Asian trading.
FT reports a junk debt rout sparking a 'bloodbath' for credit investors; Bloomberg says investors brace for more volatile days after the tech rout.
Bloomberg: AI enthusiasm is collapsing and Big Tech earnings made it worse; CNBC says stocks reversed from early-week gains.
OpenAI pares fundraising goal to as much as $20 billion; S&P turns negative on Meta; Intel has worst day since the 1970s.
Meta falls 6% as AI spending pushes free cash flow negative and its credit default swaps hit records; tech stocks slide.
Treasury yields sink below 5% as investors seek safety from AI fallout, MarketWatch reports.
DeepSeek reportedly raises $15 billion days after US federal restrictions.
Stocks fall as megacap earnings fail to reassure on AI; Treasuries and yen rally as havens and Chinese equities near a bear market.
Meta says it will issue a new class of non-voting shares, trading from 2027, to fund AI initiatives, acquisitions and pay.
SpaceX shares jump about 10% on earnings and Tesla merger talk, while its bonds weaken on debt fears.
Nebius says AI computing prices are rising as investors question neocloud debt and economics.
Stocks rise as strong tech earnings revive the AI trade after last week's selloff; oil gains.
Australian data center operator NextDC plunges about 40% after cutting its earnings forecast over power delays.
Credit-risk gauges for major tech companies hit fresh highs as investors brace for post-earnings bond sales.
China defends DeepSeek and warns of possible retaliation after the DHS order removing it from federal systems.
South Korean data centre builder Elice tumbles 32% on its trading debut, adding to AI valuation concerns.
SoftBank's credit default swaps hit their highest in nearly four years on AI funding strain; FT reports surging default-swap trading on Big Tech.
Futures edge higher after a chipmaker rally helps the Nasdaq 100 recover from its worst week since April 2025.
CoreWeave bonds slip into distressed territory, becoming a wider AI industry problem, The Verge reports.
DHS order removing DeepSeek from federal systems is published in the Federal Register.

storylines.title: Fed under Warsh weighs further hikes
storylines.summary: After a September hike, the Fed under Chairman Kevin Warsh left rates unchanged in October, NPR reports, as GDP and prices both rose. Kalshi traders now put a December 25bp hike at 70%. Housing data is weak.

events.text: NPR: GDP growth is up but so are prices; interest rates are staying the same for now, with midterms ahead.
Axios: traders bet oil prices stay elevated longer, threatening to prolong inflation pressure.
CNBC reports housing data worsened in September as the Fed weighs more rate hikes; Axios says homebuilder sentiment is at a 14-year low.
MarketWatch says the October decision is a closer call than markets think, weighing arguments against a hike.
Warsh says the economy has performed largely as expected since the September hike; markets expect a hold.

storylines.title: 2026 midterm elections
storylines.summary: With Election Day Tuesday, Democrats are pursuing action against Rep. Haley Stevens after her Rogers endorsement. DOJ plans to appeal the Alaska ruling. NYT/Siena polls show Democrats narrowly ahead in seven Senate races; Decision Desk HQ sees a likely House flip.

events.text: Stevens is removed from the Michigan Democratic Party, Washington Examiner reports; some House Democrats seek her removal from caucus, Axios reports.
DOJ set to appeal dismissal of its Alaska Senate certification suit, Fox News reports; Sanders calls alleged Democratic ballot-stacking 'pretty dumb'.
NYT/Siena polls show Democrats narrowly ahead in seven Senate races, mostly within margin of error; another poll finds late deciders favor Republicans.
Trump says he would become 'Mr. Veto' if Democrats win Congress; an NBC poll shows 52% prefer a Democratic Congress, 45% Republican.
A federal judge dismisses the DOJ lawsuit seeking to block certification of Alaska's Senate race if Republican Dan Sullivan loses; Sullivan says he will accept results.
Rep. Haley Stevens endorses Republican Mike Rogers in the Michigan Senate race; Democratic leaders condemn the move, and Trump praises it.
El-Sayed asks Rep. Haley Stevens to stay away from his events, a source says; a Clyburn adviser says he cannot disinvite her from a Sunday event.
DOJ seeks to isolate Alaska ballots amid a criminal probe over the two-Dan-Sullivan ballot dispute; Peltola denies involvement.
More than 50 million Americans have cast early ballots, a record, with Democrats ahead in states reporting party data.
Federal judge orders halt to noncitizen voting investigation in nine states, citing error-filled data and intimidation of voter assistance groups.
US Attorney Bill Essayli says DOJ verified all 20,000 flagged California voter entries as noncitizens who received mail ballots.
Amy Acton calls Ramaswamy's ad despicable; Gov. DeWine urges Ramaswamy to take it down.
Utah says DOJ is sending election monitors for the Nov. 3 midterms.
Trump rallies in Clemson for Sen. Darline Graham; the Guardian reports he praised a supporter who allegedly punched a protester.
Michigan and Kansas Senate candidates hold final debates; Kansas race is tighter than Republicans anticipated.
Democratic groups sue the Trump administration, alleging it uses unfounded fraud claims and prosecution threats to pressure election officials.
Trump heads to South Carolina for Sen. Darline Graham; Axios reports Senate Republicans weigh more money for Mississippi, South Carolina and Kansas.
NPR poll shows record support for Democratic congressional candidates; FT reports a large Republican spending advantage.
Vance says he is disgusted by Republicans criticizing Ramaswamy's ad featuring Amy Acton's estranged mother.
Wedgewood Polls admits fabricating survey data; FCC chair Carr warns broadcasters about false polls.

storylines.title: US-Iran war and oil prices
storylines.summary: Qatar is leading intense mediation to prevent possible US attacks on Iran after the midterms; Gulf states are braced for escalation. Oil fell on a report Trump will give diplomacy more time, while Netanyahu presses him to strike.

events.text: Oil declines after a report Trump wants to give Iran diplomacy more time before possibly resuming strikes after the midterms, Bloomberg says.
FT: Gulf states brace for escalation between the US-Israel alliance and Iran; diplomats warn renewed conflict would be more damaging than earlier rounds.
Gulf leaders meet in Qatar as mediators await Washington's reply to an Iranian proposal involving $6 billion in assets and reopening Hormuz.
Axios: Trump has a frank call with Netanyahu about how quickly to return to combat; Netanyahu presses for strikes.
Trump says the US is not in much of a hurry for an Iran deal; Araghchi says Iran and Qatar have a plan to reopen Hormuz in two days.
Qatari mediators hold 12-plus hours of talks in Tehran to restart US-Iran negotiations; talks continue in Doha.
Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei orders an immediate response without geographical limits to any US or Israeli attack.
Oil jumps to a five-month high as Iran's IRGC says it hit four vessels in the northern Gulf and three ships struck mines near Hormuz.
NPR source says the US and Israel are planning a possible attack on Iran in early November, after the midterms; Iran says it is prepared.
Houthi attack on King Fahd airport kills one and wounds eight; a drone attack on Aramco's Shaybah oilfield reportedly kills two; oil rises.
State Department orders nonemergency personnel and families to leave Saudi Arabia as Houthi attacks continue; Fox reports Trump weighs strikes on Houthis.
Iran says it is determined to keep its uranium and had nothing new for Washington after reported mediator proposals.
Dozens of Israeli fighter jets fly a sortie to the Iranian border, per Israeli and US officials, Axios reports.
Macron makes a surprise visit to Riyadh as France secures extra diesel supplies.
United Airlines forecasts weak Q4 earnings as jet fuel costs surge.
FT reports Netanyahu is pushing to resume strikes on Iran; Israel held off earlier plans as Trump rules out an attack before the midterms.
Netanyahu says he discussed eliminating Iran's regime with Trump; Sen. Rick Scott backs renewed bombing if it speeds regime change.
Pentagon weighs force posture and the cost of rebuilding Middle East bases, a senior defense official says.
UK to deploy RAF Typhoons on defensive missions over Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks.
Vance says he is 'not getting involved' when asked whether he endorses Netanyahu, a day after Trump's endorsement.

storylines.title: Binance $6.3 billion hack
storylines.summary: A record $6.3 billion hack of Binance, blamed by the FBI on North Korean group TraderTraitor, led to suspended withdrawals. Binance resumed phased withdrawals and says 90% of losses are covered; users have since withdrawn $3.6 billion, the BBC reports.

events.text: Binance users withdraw $3.6 billion after the exchange resumes transactions following the largest-ever crypto hack, the BBC reports.
Binance resumes phased withdrawals; TechCrunch reports 95% of stolen assets covered, while Binance's own figure reported elsewhere is 90%.
Binance says 90% of losses are covered and withdrawals resume Sunday; FBI says North Korea-backed TraderTraitor is behind the attack.

storylines.title: Israel election deadlock
storylines.summary: Israel's election produced a deadlock, with an Arab coalition holding the balance of power after winning a record number of seats. Netanyahu claims the vote was 'stolen'; the election body says results stand.

events.text: Israel's election body says the deadlocked result will stand even if foreign-interference claims are proven, as Netanyahu alleges the election was 'stolen'.
Arab coalition leader Yousef Jabareen says he is ready to join the opposition bloc to oust Netanyahu after record seat gains, the Guardian reports.
